name: Pixel Sorting
basis: runs of pixels sorted by a key (how)

lumenary.blurb: Streaks of pixels re-ordered by brightness, so highlights melt into long smears.

facts.bestOn: Pictures with a bright sky or large smooth areas

why: Sorting is the most ordinary operation in computing, and it does something strange to a picture: it keeps the colours but destroys the positions. If only the pixels inside a certain brightness range are sorted, the rest of the picture holds its structure while the chosen parts melt into long, tidy streaks.
how: Walk along a column (or row) of the picture.
Start collecting pixels when the brightness enters the chosen band.
Stop when it leaves the band or when the run reaches a random cap, the streak length.
Sort the collected pixels by the chosen key: brightness, hue, red or blue.
Write them back in sorted order, leaving every pixel outside the band untouched.
history: Pixel sorting was popularised around 2010 by the artist Kim Asendorf, who published a short script that sorted rows and columns of photographs. It has since become one of the signatures of glitch art. The idea was never new in mathematics, but it was a happy accident to point it at pictures.
terms: A cut-off value that decides whether a pixel is included.
The property pixels are ordered by, such as brightness or hue.
A stretch of consecutive pixels that is sorted together.
paragraphs: Pixel sorting takes runs of pixels and puts them in order. Walk along a column (or row); wherever the brightness is inside the chosen band, start collecting pixels, and stop when it leaves the band or when the run reaches a random cap (the streak length). Sort the collected pixels by a key, and write them back in sorted order. Pixels outside the band are never touched, so a sharp structure remains in the places the sorting skips.

The key can be brightness, red, blue or hue. Bright regions sorted from dark to light grow a smear that gets brighter as it goes; reversing the order flips the direction. The cost is a sort per run, so it is O(N log n) for runs of length n.

equations.note: Pixels in the brightness band [ℓ, h], up to a maximum length.

presets.text: Sort horizontally by hue for rainbow smears.
Long streaks from a low threshold melt the whole sky.
Reverse the order to flip the direction of the smear.
